source.primary_witnesses: MT BHS Codex Leningradensis — entirely Aramaic. SECONDARY: 4Q112 (Daniela) preserves fragments. The OG + Theodotion-Greek insert the long Prayer of Azariah + Song of the Three Young Men between v 23 and v 24 of MT — this expansion is OUTSIDE Ship A scope; only the MT 30-verse form is included here. TERTIARY: Greek versions consulted only where text-critically significant.

source.paleography_note: CHAPTER 3 — ARAMAIC, the fiery-furnace narrative. Daniel himself is conspicuously absent; the three companions are the focus. Repetition + cumulative-list style (the six musical instruments listed four times in vv 5, 7, 10, 15; the eight official-titles listed three times in vv 2, 3, 27) is characteristic of court-tale oral-tradition style. The 'fourth one like a son of the gods' (v 25) is theologically + cross-corpus dense. The OG + Theodotion expansions (Prayer of Azariah + Song of the Three) are OUTSIDE Ship A scope but their existence demonstrates the early-period tradition of liturgical-expansion at this narrative moment.

verses.text: נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֣ר מַלְכָּ֗א עֲבַד֙ צְלֵ֣ם דִּֽי־דְהַ֔ב רוּמֵהּ֙ אַמִּ֣ין שִׁתִּ֔ין פְּתָיֵ֖הּ אַמִּ֣ין שִׁ֑ת אֲקִימֵהּ֙ בְּבִקְעַ֣ת דּוּרָ֔א בִּמְדִינַ֖ת בָּבֶֽל׃
verses.translit: Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar malkāʾ ʿăḇaḏ ṣəlēm dî-ḏəhaḇ rūmēh ʾammîn šittîn pəṯāyēh ʾammîn šit ʾăqîmēh bə-ḇiqʿaṯ Dūrāʾ bi-mḏînaṯ Bāḇel
verses.notes: **King Nebuchadnezzar made an image of gold, sixty cubits high and six cubits wide; he set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.** **NUMEROLOGICAL READING**: 60 cubits × 6 cubits — the 6-6 measurement anticipates the 666-number-of-the-beast tradition (Rev 13:18) which Christian apocalyptic tradition reads as deriving from this Daniel statue. The image-of-gold callback to the head-of-gold (Dan 2:38) frames Nebuchadnezzar as enlarging the dream-image into a full colossus — a literalist political-theological inversion of the dream's message (where the gold head was already merely the first kingdom). The plain of Dura: location uncertain; possibly Tell Dēr 18 km south of Babylon.

verses.text: וּנְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֣ר מַלְכָּ֡א שְׁלַ֡ח לְמִכְנַ֣שׁ לַֽאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּ֡א סִגְנַיָּ֣א וּֽפַחֲוָתָ֡א אֲדַרְגָּזְרַיָּא֩ גְדָ֨בְרַיָּ֤א דְּתָבְרַיָּא֙ תִּפְתָּיֵ֔א וְכֹ֖ל שִׁלְטֹנֵ֣י מְדִֽינָתָ֑א לְמֵתֵא֙ לַחֲנֻכַּ֣ת צַלְמָ֔א דִּ֥י הֲקֵ֖ים נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֥ר מַלְכָּֽא׃
verses.translit: ū-Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar malkāʾ šəlaḥ lə-miḵnaš la-ʾăḥašdarpənayyāʾ siḡnayyāʾ ū-paḥăwāṯāʾ ʾădargāzərayyāʾ ḡəḏāḇərayyāʾ dəṯāḇərayyāʾ tiftāyēʾ wə-ḵōl šilṭōnê mədînāṯāʾ lə-mēṯēʾ la-ḥănukkaṯ ṣalmāʾ dī hăqêm Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar malkāʾ
verses.notes: **Nebuchadnezzar the king sent to gather the satraps, prefects, governors, counselors, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the officials of the provinces to come to the dedication of the image which Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up.** **EIGHT OFFICIAL TITLES — PERSIAN-PERIOD VOCABULARY**: אֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּא (ʾăḥašdarpənayyāʾ 'satraps' from Old Persian *xšaçapāvan-); סִגְנַיָּא (siḡnayyāʾ 'prefects' from Akkadian šaknu); פַּחֲוָתָא (paḥăwāṯāʾ 'governors' from Akkadian pāḫatu); אֲדַרְגָּזְרַיָּא (ʾădargāzərayyāʾ 'counselors' from Old Persian *handar-gazara-); גְדָבְרַיָּא (ḡəḏāḇərayyāʾ 'treasurers' from Old Persian *ganza-bara-); דְּתָבְרַיָּא (dəṯāḇərayyāʾ 'judges' from Old Persian *dāta-bara-); תִּפְתָּיֵא (tiftāyēʾ 'magistrates' uncertain). **The Persian-loanword density is diagnostic of post-exilic / Persian-period composition.** This eight-title list repeats verbatim in v 3 + v 27.

verses.text: בֵּאדַ֡יִן מִֽתְכַּנְּשִׁ֡ין אֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּ֡א סִגְנַיָּ֣א וּֽפַחֲוָתָ֡א אֲדַרְגָּזְרַיָּ֣א גְדָבְרַיָּא֩ דְּתָ֨בְרַיָּ֜א תִּפְתָּיֵ֗א וְכֹל֙ שִׁלְטֹנֵ֣י מְדִֽינָתָ֔א לַחֲנֻכַּ֣ת צַלְמָ֔א דִּ֥י הֲקֵ֖ים נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֣ר מַלְכָּ֑א וקאמין וְקָֽיְמִין֙ לָקֳבֵ֣ל צַלְמָ֔א דִּ֥י הֲקֵ֖ים נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּֽר׃
verses.translit: bēʾḏayin miṯkannəšîn ʾăḥašdarpənayyāʾ siḡnayyāʾ ū-paḥăwāṯāʾ ʾădargāzərayyāʾ ḡəḏāḇərayyāʾ dəṯāḇərayyāʾ tiftāyēʾ wə-ḵōl šilṭōnê mədînāṯāʾ la-ḥănukkaṯ ṣalmāʾ dī hăqêm Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar malkāʾ wə-qāyəmîn lā-qoḇēl ṣalmāʾ dī hăqêm Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar
verses.notes: **Then the satraps, the prefects, the governors, the counselors, the treasurers, the judges, the magistrates, and all the officials of the provinces gathered together for the dedication of the image which Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up; they stood before the image which Nebuchadnezzar had set up.** **CEREMONIAL REDUNDANCY**: the verbatim repetition of vv 2-3 (and the lists in vv 5, 7, 10, 15) is oral-literary style intensification — the cumulative effect signals totalitarian-imperial-cultic-ceremony aesthetics. Note the qere-ketiv variant (וקאמין/וְקָיְמִין) — the qere is preferred.

verses.text: וְכָרוֹזָ֖א קָרֵ֣א בְחָ֑יִל לְכ֤וֹן אָֽמְרִין֙ עַֽמְמַיָּ֔א אֻמַּיָּ֖א וְלִשָּׁנַיָּֽא׃
verses.translit: wə-ḵārōzāʾ qārēʾ ḇə-ḥāyil lə-ḵōn ʾāmərîn ʿammə-mayyāʾ ʾummayyāʾ wə-liššānayyāʾ
verses.notes: **Then the herald cried aloud: 'To you it is commanded, O peoples, nations, and languages.'** **KEY TRIPARTITE FORMULA**: עַמְמַיָּא אֻמַּיָּא וְלִשָּׁנַיָּא ('peoples, nations, languages') — appears here, 3:7, 3:29, 4:1, 5:19, 6:25 and is a recurring Daniel-Aramaic universalizing formula. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Rev 5:9, 7:9, 10:11, 11:9, 13:7, 14:6, 17:15 ('every tribe and language and people and nation') — Revelation's universalizing-people-formulae directly inherit from Daniel's Aramaic. **TERM**: כָּרוֹזָא (kārōzāʾ 'herald') — Persian loanword.

verses.text: בְּעִדָּנָ֡א דִּֽי־תִשְׁמְע֡וּן קָ֣ל קַרְנָ֣א מַ֠שְׁרוֹקִיתָא קיתרס קַתְר֨וֹס סַבְּכָ֤א פְּסַנְתֵּרִין֙ סוּמְפֹּ֣נְיָ֔ה וְכֹ֖ל זְנֵ֣י זְמָרָ֑א תִּפְּל֤וּן וְתִסְגְּדוּן֙ לְצֶ֣לֶם דַּהֲבָ֔א דִּ֥י הֲקֵ֖ים נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֥ר מַלְכָּֽא׃
verses.translit: bə-ʿiddānāʾ dî-ṯišməʿūn qāl qarnāʾ mašrōqîṯāʾ qaṯrōs sabbəḵāʾ pəsantērîn sūmpōnəyāh wə-ḵōl zənê zəmārāʾ tippəlūn wə-ṯisgədūn lə-ṣelem dahăḇāʾ dī hăqêm Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar malkāʾ
verses.notes: **'At the time you hear the sound of the horn, pipe, lyre, trigon, harp, bagpipe, and every kind of music, you are to fall down and worship the golden image which King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.'** **SIX MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS — DIAGNOSTIC FOR HELLENISTIC-ERA COMPOSITION**: three are Greek loanwords — קַתְרוֹס (qaṯrōs / קיתרס qere — Greek κιθάρα *kithara*), פְּסַנְתֵּרִין (pəsantērîn — Greek ψαλτήριον *psaltērion*), סוּמְפֹּנְיָה (sūmpōnəyāh — Greek συμφωνία *symphōnia*). **The Greek loanwords are the strongest internal evidence dating the Aramaic core of Daniel to the Hellenistic period (post-330 BCE), per Collins 1993 + Newsom 2014.** Note the qere-ketiv variant for קַתְרוֹס (qere preferred over ketiv קיתרס).

verses.text: וּמַן־דִּי־לָ֥א יִפֵּ֖ל וְיִסְגֻּ֑ד בַּהּ־שַׁעֲתָ֣א יִתְרְמֵ֔א לְגֽוֹא־אַתּ֥וּן נוּרָ֖א יָקִֽדְתָּֽא׃
verses.translit: ū-man-dî-lāʾ yippēl wə-yisgud bah-šaʿăṯāʾ yiṯrəmēʾ lə-ḡōʾ-ʾattūn nūrāʾ yāqîḏtāʾ
verses.notes: **'And whoever does not fall down and worship shall immediately be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace.'** **THE PENALTY**: foundational martyrdom-test text. **TERM**: אַתּוּן נוּרָא (ʾattūn nūrāʾ 'furnace of fire') — Akkadian-derived term for a kiln/smelting-furnace. **CROSS-CORPUS**: Rev 20:14-15 'lake of fire' inherits the imagery; cf. Matt 13:42, 50 ('furnace of fire' — *kaminos tou pyros*, Jesus' eschatological-judgment idiom directly cites Dan 3:6 LXX).

verses.text: כָּל־קֳבֵ֣ל דְּנָ֡ה בֵּהּ־זִמְנָ֡א כְּדִ֣י שָֽׁמְעִ֣ין כָּֽל־עַמְמַיָּ֡א קָ֣ל קַרְנָא֩ מַשְׁר֨וֹקִיתָ֜א קיתרס קַתְר֤וֹס שַׂבְּכָא֙ פְּסַנְטֵרִ֔ין וְכֹ֖ל זְנֵ֣י זְמָרָ֑א נָֽפְלִ֨ין כָּֽל־עַֽמְמַיָּ֜א אֻמַּיָּ֣א וְלִשָּׁנַיָּ֗א סָֽגְדִין֙ לְצֶ֣לֶם דַּהֲבָ֔א דִּ֥י הֲקֵ֖ים נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֥ר מַלְכָּֽא׃
verses.translit: kol-qŏḇēl dənāh bēh-zimnāʾ kə-ḏî šāməʿîn kol-ʿammə-mayyāʾ qāl qarnāʾ mašrōqîṯāʾ qaṯrōs śabbəḵāʾ pəsanṭērîn wə-ḵōl zənê zəmārāʾ nāpəlîn kol-ʿammə-mayyāʾ ʾummayyāʾ wə-liššānayyāʾ sāḡəḏîn lə-ṣelem dahăḇāʾ dī hăqêm Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar malkāʾ
verses.notes: **Therefore, as soon as all the peoples heard the sound of the horn, pipe, lyre, trigon, harp, and every kind of music, all the peoples, nations, and languages fell down and worshiped the golden image which King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.** Refrain-repetition continues; here the instrument-list is shortened (five not six — note the absence of סוּמְפֹּנְיָה sūmpōnəyāh).

verses.text: כָּל־קֳבֵ֤ל דְּנָה֙ בֵּהּ־זִמְנָ֔א קְרִ֖בוּ גֻּבְרִ֣ין כַּשְׂדָּאִ֑ין וַאֲכַ֥לוּ קַרְצֵיהֹ֖ון דִּ֥י יְהוּדָיֵֽא׃
verses.translit: kol-qŏḇēl dənāh bēh-zimnāʾ qəriḇū guḇrîn kaśdāʾîn wa-ʾăḵalū qarṣêhōn dī yəhūḏāyêʾ
verses.notes: **Therefore at that time certain Chaldeans came forward and brought accusation against the Jews.** **IDIOM**: אֲכַל קַרְצֵיהוֹן (ʾăḵalū qarṣêhōn 'they ate their pieces' = 'they slandered, denounced') — Akkadian-derived idiom for malicious denunciation. **The 'Chaldeans-versus-Jews' framing**: the polemical encoding of mantic-class rivalry as ethnic-religious antagonism.

verses.text: עֲנוֹ֙ וְאָ֣מְרִ֔ין לִנְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֖ר מַלְכָּ֑א מַלְכָּ֖א לְעָלְמִ֥ין חֱיִֽי׃
verses.translit: ʿănō wə-ʾāmərîn li-Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar malkāʾ malkāʾ lə-ʿāləmîn ḥĕyî
verses.notes: **They answered and said to King Nebuchadnezzar: 'O king, live forever!'** Standard court-greeting formula (cf. 2:4, 5:10, 6:7, 6:22).

verses.text: אנתה אַ֣נְתְּ מַלְכָּא֮ שָׂ֣מְתָּ טְּעֵם֒ דִּ֣י כָל־אֱנָ֡שׁ דִּֽי־יִשְׁמַ֡ע קָ֣ל קַרְנָ֣א מַ֠שְׁרֹקִיתָא קַתְר֨וֹס שַׂבְּכָ֤א פְסַנְתֵּרִין֙ וסיפניה וְסוּפֹּ֣נְיָ֔ה וְכֹ֖ל זְנֵ֣י זְמָרָ֑א יִפֵּ֥ל וְיִסְגֻּ֖ד לְצֶ֥לֶם דַּהֲבָֽא׃
verses.translit: ʾant malkāʾ śāmtā ṭəʿēm dī ḵol-ʾĕnāš dî-yišmaʿ qāl qarnāʾ mašrōqîṯāʾ qaṯrōs śabbəḵāʾ pəsantērîn wə-sūppōnəyāh wə-ḵōl zənê zəmārāʾ yippēl wə-yisgud lə-ṣelem dahăḇāʾ
verses.notes: **'You, O king, have made a decree that every man who hears the sound of the horn, pipe, lyre, trigon, harp, and bagpipe, and every kind of music, shall fall down and worship the golden image.'** Note qere-ketiv variants — אנתה / אַנְתְּ ('you' — qere) + וסיפניה / וְסוּפֹּנְיָה (instrument name — qere).

verses.text: וּמַן־דִּי־לָ֥א יִפֵּ֖ל וְיִסְגֻּ֑ד יִתְרְמֵ֕א לְגֽוֹא־אַתּ֥וּן נוּרָ֖א יָקִֽדְתָּֽא׃
verses.translit: ū-man-dî-lāʾ yippēl wə-yisgud yiṯrəmēʾ lə-ḡōʾ-ʾattūn nūrāʾ yāqîḏtāʾ
verses.notes: **'And whoever does not fall down and worship shall be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace.'**

verses.text: אִיתַ֞י גֻּבְרִ֣ין יְהוּדָאיִ֗ן דִּֽי־מַנִּ֤יתָ יָתְהוֹן֙ עַל־עֲבִידַת֙ מְדִינַ֣ת בָּבֶ֔ל שַׁדְרַ֥ךְ מֵישַׁ֖ךְ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֑וֹ גֻּבְרַיָּ֣א אִלֵּ֗ךְ לָא־שָׂ֨מֽוּ עליך עֲלָ֤ךְ מַלְכָּא֙ טְעֵ֔ם לאלהיך לֵֽאלָהָךְ֙ לָ֣א פָלְחִ֔ין וּלְצֶ֧לֶם דַּהֲבָ֛א דִּ֥י הֲקֵ֖ימְתָּ לָ֥א סָגְדִֽין׃
verses.translit: ʾîtay guḇrîn yəhūḏāʾyîn dî-mannîṯā yāṯhōn ʿal-ʿăḇîḏaṯ mədînaṯ Bāḇel Šadraḵ Mêšaḵ wa-ʿĂḇēḏ Nəḡō guḇrayyāʾ ʾillēḵ lāʾ-śāmū ʿălāḵ malkāʾ ṭəʿēm lê-ʾlāhāḵ lāʾ pāləḥîn ū-lə-ṣelem dahăḇāʾ dī hăqêmtā lāʾ sāḡəḏîn
verses.notes: **'There are certain Jews whom you have appointed over the affairs of the province of Babylon — Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. These men, O king, pay no heed to you; they do not serve your gods or worship the golden image which you have set up.'** **THE DENUNCIATION**: the three are identified by their Babylonian throne-names — the same names imposed on them in 1:7 are now used against them by the Chaldean accusers. The literary irony: the assimilation-renaming becomes the identification-label for resistance. Note qere-ketiv: עליך/עֲלָךְ (qere) and לאלהיך/לֵאלָהָךְ (qere).

verses.text: בֵּאדַ֤יִן נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר֙ בִּרְגַ֣ז וַחֲמָ֔ה אֲמַר֙ לְהַיְתָיָ֔ה לְשַׁדְרַ֥ךְ מֵישַׁ֖ךְ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֑וֹ בֵּאדַ֙יִן֙ גֻּבְרַיָּ֣א אִלֵּ֔ךְ הֵיתָ֖יוּ קֳדָ֥ם מַלְכָּֽא׃
verses.translit: bēʾḏayin Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar bi-rḡaz wa-ḥămāh ʾămar lə-haytāyāh lə-Šadraḵ Mêšaḵ wa-ʿĂḇēḏ Nəḡō bēʾḏayin guḇrayyāʾ ʾillēḵ hêtāyū qŏdām malkāʾ
verses.notes: **Then Nebuchadnezzar in furious rage commanded that Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego be brought; they were brought before the king.**

verses.text: עָנֵ֤ה נְבֻֽכַדְנֶצַּר֙ וְאָמַ֣ר לְה֔וֹן הַצְדָּ֕א שַׁדְרַ֥ךְ מֵישַׁ֖ךְ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֑וֹ לֵֽאלָהַ֗י לָ֤א אִֽיתֵיכוֹן֙ פָּֽלְחִ֔ין וּלְצֶ֧לֶם דַּהֲבָ֛א דִּ֥י הֲקֵ֖ימֶת לָ֥א סָגְדִֽין׃
verses.translit: ʿănēh Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar wə-ʾāmar lə-hōn ha-ṣəḏāʾ Šadraḵ Mêšaḵ wa-ʿĂḇēḏ Nəḡō lê-ʾlāhay lāʾ ʾîṯêḵōn pāləḥîn ū-lə-ṣelem dahăḇāʾ dī hăqêmeṯ lāʾ sāḡəḏîn
verses.notes: **Nebuchadnezzar said to them: 'Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, that you do not serve my gods or worship the golden image which I have set up?'**

verses.text: כְּעַ֞ן הֵ֧ן אִֽיתֵיכ֣וֹן עֲתִידִ֗ין דִּ֣י בְעִדָּנָ֡א דִּֽי־תִשְׁמְע֡וּן קָ֣ל קַרְנָ֣א מַשְׁרוֹקִיתָ֣א קַתְר֣וֹס שַׂבְּכָ֡א פְּסַנְתֵּרִין֩ וְסוּמְפֹּ֨נְיָ֜ה וְכֹ֣ל ׀ זְנֵ֣י זְמָרָ֗א תִּפְּל֣וּן וְתִסְגְּדוּן֮ לְצַלְמָ֣א דִֽי־עַבְדֵת֒ וְהֵן֙ לָ֣א תִסְגְּד֔וּן בַּהּ־שַׁעֲתָ֣ה תִתְרְמ֔וֹן לְגֽוֹא־אַתּ֥וּן נוּרָ֖א יָקִֽדְתָּ֑א וּמַן־ה֣וּא אֱלָ֔הּ דִּ֥י יְשֵֽׁיזְבִנְכ֖וֹן מִן־יְדָֽי׃
verses.translit: kəʿan hēn ʾîṯêḵōn ʿăṯîḏîn dī ḇə-ʿiddānāʾ dî-ṯišməʿūn qāl qarnāʾ mašrōqîṯāʾ qaṯrōs śabbəḵāʾ pəsantērîn wə-sūmpōnəyāh wə-ḵōl zənê zəmārāʾ tippəlūn wə-ṯisgədūn lə-ṣalmāʾ ḏî-ʿaḇḏēṯ wə-hēn lāʾ ṯisgədūn bah-šaʿăṯāh ṯiṯrəmōn lə-ḡōʾ-ʾattūn nūrāʾ yāqîḏtāʾ ū-man-hūʾ ʾĕlāh dī yəšêzəḇinḵōn min-yəḏāy
verses.notes: **'Now if you are ready... and worship the image which I have made, well and good; but if you do not worship, you shall immediately be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace; and who is the god that will deliver you out of my hands?'** **THE BLASPHEMY-QUESTION**: 'who is the god that will deliver you out of my hands?' is direct counter-claim to YHWH's covenant-rescue identity. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Exod 5:2 (Pharaoh: 'who is YHWH that I should obey his voice?'); cf. 2 Kgs 18:33-35 (Rabshakeh: 'has any of the gods of the nations ever delivered his land from the king of Assyria?'). The narrative-pattern: king sets himself against YHWH and is publicly answered.

verses.text: עֲנ֗וֹ שַׁדְרַ֤ךְ מֵישַׁךְ֙ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֔וֹ וְאָמְרִ֖ין לְמַלְכָּ֑א נְבֽוּכַדְנֶצַּ֔ר לָֽא־חַשְׁחִ֨ין אֲנַ֧חְנָה עַל־דְּנָ֛ה פִּתְגָ֖ם לַהֲתָבוּתָֽךְ׃
verses.translit: ʿănō Šadraḵ Mêšaḵ wa-ʿĂḇēḏ Nəḡō wə-ʾāmərîn lə-malkāʾ Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar lāʾ-ḥašḥîn ʾănaḥnāh ʿal-dənāh piṯḡām la-hăṯāḇūṯāḵ
verses.notes: **Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego answered the king: 'O Nebuchadnezzar, we have no need to answer you in this matter.'**

verses.text: הֵ֣ן אִיתַ֗י אֱלָהַ֙נָא֙ דִּֽי־אֲנַ֣חְנָא פָֽלְחִ֔ין יָכִ֖ל לְשֵׁיזָבוּתַ֑נָא מִן־אַתּ֨וּן נוּרָ֧א יָקִֽדְתָּ֛א וּמִן־יְדָ֥ךְ מַלְכָּ֖א יְשֵׁיזִֽב׃
verses.translit: hēn ʾîtay ʾĕlāhanāʾ dî-ʾănaḥnāʾ pāləḥîn yāḵîl lə-šêzāḇūṯanāʾ min-ʾattūn nūrāʾ yāqîḏtāʾ ū-min-yəḏāḵ malkāʾ yəšêziḇ
verses.notes: **'If our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, he will deliver us out of your hand, O king.'**

verses.text: וְהֵ֣ן לָ֔א יְדִ֥יעַ לֶהֱוֵא־לָ֖ךְ מַלְכָּ֑א דִּ֤י לֵֽאלָהָךְ֙ לָא־איתינא אִיתַ֣נָא פָֽלְחִ֔ין וּלְצֶ֧לֶם דַּהֲבָ֛א דִּ֥י הֲקֵ֖ימְתָּ לָ֥א נִסְגֻּֽד׃
verses.translit: wə-hēn lāʾ yəḏîaʿ lehĕwēʾ-lāḵ malkāʾ dī lê-ʾlāhāḵ lāʾ-ʾîṯanāʾ pāləḥîn ū-lə-ṣelem dahăḇāʾ dī hăqêmtā lāʾ nisgud
verses.notes: **'But if not, be it known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden image which you have set up.'** **THE 'BUT IF NOT' MARTYRDOM CONFESSION**: foundational martyrdom-theology — fidelity even without guarantee of rescue. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Job 13:15 ('though he slay me, yet will I trust him'); cf. 2 Macc 7 (the seven brothers); cf. Heb 11:35-38 (the 'unrescued martyrs' catalogue).

verses.text: בֵּאדַ֨יִן נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֜ר הִתְמְלִ֣י חֱמָ֗א וּצְלֵ֤ם אַנְפּ֙וֹהִי֙ אֶשְׁתַּנִּ֔י עַל־שַׁדְרַ֥ךְ מֵישַׁ֖ךְ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֑וֹ עָנֵ֤ה וְאָמַר֙ לְמֵזֵ֣א לְאַתּוּנָ֔א חַ֨ד־שִׁבְעָ֔ה עַ֛ל דִּ֥י חֲזֵ֖ה לְמֵזְיֵֽהּ׃
verses.translit: bēʾḏayin Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar hiṯməlî ḥĕmāʾ ū-ṣəlēm ʾanpōhî ʾeštannî ʿal-Šadraḵ Mêšaḵ wa-ʿĂḇēḏ Nəḡō ʿănēh wə-ʾāmar lə-mēzēʾ lə-ʾattūnāʾ ḥaḏ-šiḇʿāh ʿal dī ḥăzēh lə-mēzəyēh
verses.notes: **Then Nebuchadnezzar was filled with fury, and the expression of his face was changed against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego; he ordered the furnace heated seven times more than usual.** **NUMEROLOGICAL DETAIL**: 'seven times' (חַד־שִׁבְעָה ḥaḏ-šiḇʿāh) — perfect-intensity number; serves the narrative-irony when the very intensification fails to harm the three (vv 25-27).

verses.text: וּלְגֻבְרִ֤ין גִּבָּֽרֵי־חַ֙יִל֙ דִּ֣י בְחַיְלֵ֔הּ אֲמַר֙ לְכַפָּתָ֔ה לְשַׁדְרַ֥ךְ מֵישַׁ֖ךְ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֑וֹ לְמִרְמֵ֕א לְאַתּ֥וּן נוּרָ֖א יָקִֽדְתָּֽא׃
verses.translit: ū-lə-ḡuḇrîn gibbārê-ḥayil dī ḇə-ḥaylēh ʾămar lə-ḵappāṯāh lə-Šadraḵ Mêšaḵ wa-ʿĂḇēḏ Nəḡō lə-mirmēʾ lə-ʾattūn nūrāʾ yāqîḏtāʾ
verses.notes: **He ordered some of the mightiest men in his army to bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and cast them into the burning fiery furnace.**

verses.text: בֵּאדַ֜יִן גֻּבְרַיָּ֣א אִלֵּ֗ךְ כְּפִ֙תוּ֙ בְּסַרְבָּלֵיהוֹן֙ פטישיהון פַּטָּשֵׁיה֔וֹן וְכַרְבְּלָתְה֖וֹן וּלְבֻשֵׁיה֑וֹן וּרְמִ֕יו לְגוֹא־אַתּ֥וּן נוּרָ֖א יָקִֽדְתָּֽא׃
verses.translit: bēʾḏayin guḇrayyāʾ ʾillēḵ kəpîṯū bə-sarbālêhōn paṭṭāšêhōn wə-ḵarbəlāṯəhōn ū-ləḇušêhōn ū-rəmîw lə-ḡōʾ-ʾattūn nūrāʾ yāqîḏtāʾ
verses.notes: **Then these men were bound in their cloaks, their tunics, their headgear, and their other garments, and they were cast into the midst of the burning fiery furnace.** **PERSIAN-PERIOD CLOTHING VOCABULARY**: סַרְבָּל (sarbāl), פַּטָּש (paṭṭāš), כַּרְבְּלָה (karbəlāh) — all Persian/Akkadian-derived clothing terms; the bilingual ketiv-qere variant at פטישיהון/פַּטָּשֵׁיהוֹן is preserved.

verses.text: כָּל־קֳבֵ֣ל דְּנָ֗ה מִן־דִּ֞י מִלַּ֤ת מַלְכָּא֙ מַחְצְפָ֔ה וְאַתּוּנָ֖א אֵזֵ֣ה יַתִּ֑ירָא גֻּבְרַיָּ֣א אִלֵּ֗ךְ דִּ֤י הַסִּ֙קוּ֙ לְשַׁדְרַ֤ךְ מֵישַׁךְ֙ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֔וֹ קַטִּ֣ל הִמּ֔וֹן שְׁבִיבָ֖א דִּ֥י נוּרָֽא׃
verses.translit: kol-qŏḇēl dənāh min-dī millat malkāʾ maḥṣəpāh wə-ʾattūnāʾ ʾêzēh yattîrāʾ guḇrayyāʾ ʾillēḵ dī hassiqū lə-Šadraḵ Mêšaḵ wa-ʿĂḇēḏ Nəḡō qaṭṭil himmōn šəḇîḇāʾ dī nūrāʾ
verses.notes: **Because the king's order was urgent and the furnace very hot, the flame of the fire killed those men who took up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.** Ironic-reversal: the very executioners die from the heat that fails to harm the intended victims.

verses.text: וְגֻבְרַיָּ֤א אִלֵּךְ֙ תְּלָ֣תֵּה֔וֹן שַׁדְרַ֥ךְ מֵישַׁ֖ךְ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֑וֹ נְפַ֛לוּ לְגֽוֹא־אַתּוּן־נוּרָ֥א יָֽקִדְתָּ֖א מְכַפְּתִֽין׃
verses.translit: wə-ḡuḇrayyāʾ ʾillēḵ təlāṯtêhōn Šadraḵ Mêšaḵ wa-ʿĂḇēḏ Nəḡō nəpalū lə-ḡōʾ-ʾattūn-nūrāʾ yāqîḏtāʾ məḵappəṯîn
verses.witness_tertiary: OG + Th insert the Prayer of Azariah + Song of the Three Young Men (additional 66 verses) between MT v 23 and v 24 — OUTSIDE Ship A scope
verses.notes: **And these three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fell down bound into the midst of the burning fiery furnace.** **CROSS-CORPUS — TEXTUAL DIVERGENCE**: the OG + Theodotion-Greek insert here the lengthy Prayer of Azariah (one of the three) + Song of the Three Young Men (a hymn sung from within the furnace) — preserved as deuterocanonical/apocryphal in Catholic + Orthodox Bibles. The MT-only-30-verse form lacks this insertion. The insertion is OUTSIDE Ship A scope, but the existence of the tradition demonstrates the early-period liturgical impulse to fill this narrative gap.

verses.text: אֱדַ֙יִן֙ נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֣ר מַלְכָּ֔א תְּוַ֖הּ וְקָ֣ם בְּהִתְבְּהָלָ֑ה עָנֵ֨ה וְאָמַ֜ר לְהַדָּֽבְר֗וֹהִי הֲלָא֩ גֻבְרִ֨ין תְּלָתָ֜א רְמֵ֤ינָא לְגוֹא־נוּרָא֙ מְכַפְּתִ֔ין עָנַ֤יִן וְאָמְרִין֙ לְמַלְכָּ֔א יַצִּיבָ֖א מַלְכָּֽא׃
verses.translit: ʾĕdayin Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar malkāʾ təwah wə-qām bə-hitbəhālāh ʿănēh wə-ʾāmar lə-haddāḇərōhî hălāʾ ḡuḇrîn təlāṯāʾ rəmênāʾ lə-ḡōʾ-nūrāʾ məḵappəṯîn ʿānayin wə-ʾāmərîn lə-malkāʾ yaṣṣîḇāʾ malkāʾ
verses.notes: **Then King Nebuchadnezzar was astonished and rose up in haste; he said to his counselors: 'Did we not cast three men bound into the fire?' They answered: 'True, O king.'**

verses.text: עָנֵ֣ה וְאָמַ֗ר הָֽא־אֲנָ֨ה חָזֵ֜ה גֻּבְרִ֣ין אַרְבְּעָ֗ה שְׁרַ֙יִן֙ מַהְלְכִ֣ין בְּגֽוֹא־נוּרָ֔א וַחֲבָ֖ל לָא־אִיתַ֣י בְּה֑וֹן וְרֵוֵהּ֙ דִּ֣י רביעיא רְֽבִיעָאָ֔ה דָּמֵ֖ה לְבַר־אֱלָהִֽין׃
verses.translit: ʿănēh wə-ʾāmar hāʾ-ʾănāh ḥāzēh guḇrîn ʾarbəʿāh šərayin mahləḵîn bə-ḡōʾ-nūrāʾ wa-ḥăḇāl lāʾ-ʾîtay bə-hōn wə-rēwēh dī rəḇîʿāʾāh dāmēh lə-ḇar-ʾĕlāhîn
verses.notes: **He answered: 'But I see four men unbound, walking in the midst of the fire, and they are not hurt; and the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods.'** **THE FOURTH-MAN-LIKE-A-SON-OF-THE-GODS** — one of the most theologically + cross-corpus dense statements in Daniel. **KEY ARAMAIC PHRASE**: דָּמֵה לְבַר־אֱלָהִין (dāmēh lə-ḇar-ʾĕlāhîn 'resembling a son of the gods'). **CROSS-CORPUS**: (a) cf. Gen 6:2, 4 (sons of god — בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים) — the Aramaic plural בַר־אֱלָהִין is the cognate divine-being designation; (b) cf. Dan 7:13 (one like a son of man — בַר אֱנָשׁ); (c) early Christian tradition (Hippolytus, Tertullian) reads the fourth as the preincarnate Christ — a Christological reading that goes beyond the Aramaic; (d) Jewish tradition reads as an angel (probably Michael per b. Pesahim 118a); (e) Collins 1993 + Newsom 2014 treat as angelic. The phrase 'son of the gods' (with the Aramaic plural ʾĕlāhîn) is divinely-marked; the king's polytheistic framing is preserved.

verses.text: בֵּאדַ֜יִן קְרֵ֣ב נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֗ר לִתְרַע֮ אַתּ֣וּן נוּרָ֣א יָקִֽדְתָּא֒ עָנֵ֣ה וְאָמַ֗ר שַׁדְרַ֨ךְ מֵישַׁ֧ךְ וַעֲבֵד־נְג֛וֹ עַבְד֛וֹהִי דִּֽי־אֱלָהָ֥א עליא עִלָּאָ֖ה פֻּ֣קוּ וֶאֱת֑וֹ בֵּאדַ֣יִן נָֽפְקִ֗ין שַׁדְרַ֥ךְ מֵישַׁ֛ךְ וַעֲבֵ֥ד נְג֖וֹ מִן־גּ֥וֹא נוּרָֽא׃
verses.translit: bēʾḏayin qəreḇ Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar li-ṯraʿ ʾattūn nūrāʾ yāqîḏtāʾ ʿănēh wə-ʾāmar Šadraḵ Mêšaḵ wa-ʿĂḇēḏ-Nəḡō ʿaḇdōhî dî-ʾĕlāhāʾ ʿillāʾāh puqū we-ʾĕṯō bēʾḏayin nāpəqîn Šadraḵ Mêšaḵ wa-ʿĂḇēḏ Nəḡō min-gōʾ nūrāʾ
verses.notes: **Then Nebuchadnezzar came near to the door of the burning fiery furnace and said: 'Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come forth!' Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego came out of the fire.** **TITLE — אֱלָהָא עִלָּאָה (ʾĕlāhāʾ ʿillāʾāh 'Most High God')** — Aramaic equivalent of Hebrew אֵל עֶלְיוֹן (El Elyon). Appears here, 4:2, 5:18, 5:21, 7:25 (Most High in Aramaic) and is a foundational Daniel-Aramaic divine title. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Mark 5:7 (the Gerasene demoniac: 'Jesus, son of the Most High God' — υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ὑψίστου) — the NT directly inherits the Daniel-Aramaic title.

verses.text: וּ֠מִֽתְכַּנְּשִׁין אֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּ֞א סִגְנַיָּ֣א וּפַחֲוָתָא֮ וְהַדָּבְרֵ֣י מַלְכָּא֒ חָזַ֣יִן לְגֻבְרַיָּ֣א אִלֵּ֡ךְ דִּי֩ לָֽא־שְׁלֵ֨ט נוּרָ֜א בְּגֶשְׁמְה֗וֹן וּשְׂעַ֤ר רֵֽאשְׁהוֹן֙ לָ֣א הִתְחָרַ֔ךְ וְסָרְבָּלֵיה֖וֹן לָ֣א שְׁנ֑וֹ וְרֵ֣יחַ נ֔וּר לָ֥א עֲדָ֖ת בְּהֽוֹן׃
verses.translit: ū-miṯkannəšîn ʾăḥašdarpənayyāʾ siḡnayyāʾ ū-paḥăwāṯāʾ wə-haddāḇərê malkāʾ ḥāzayin lə-ḡuḇrayyāʾ ʾillēḵ dī lāʾ-šəlēṭ nūrāʾ bə-ḡešmə-hōn ū-śəʿar rēšəhōn lāʾ hiṯḥāraḵ wə-sārbālêhōn lāʾ šənō wə-rêaḥ nūr lāʾ ʿăḏāṯ bə-hōn
verses.notes: **The satraps, the prefects, the governors, and the king's counselors gathered together and saw that the fire had no power over the bodies of these men; the hair of their heads was not singed, their cloaks were not changed, and no smell of fire had come upon them.** **THE QUADRUPLE NEGATION** — bodies, hair, clothing, smell — totalizing miraculous preservation. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Isa 43:2 ('when you walk through fire you shall not be burned, the flame shall not consume you') — Daniel 3 functions as the narrative literalization of Isaiah's promise. cf. 1 Cor 3:15 (the believer's works tested by fire); cf. 1 Pet 1:7 (faith tested by fire).

verses.text: עָנֵ֨ה נְבֽוּכַדְנֶצַּ֜ר וְאָמַ֗ר בְּרִ֤יךְ אֱלָהֲהוֹן֙ דִּֽי־שַׁדְרַ֤ךְ מֵישַׁךְ֙ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֔וֹ דִּֽי־שְׁלַ֤ח מַלְאֲכֵהּ֙ וְשֵׁיזִ֣ב לְעַבְד֔וֹהִי דִּ֥י הִתְרְחִ֖צוּ עֲל֑וֹהִי וּמִלַּ֤ת מַלְכָּא֙ שַׁנִּ֔יו וִיהַ֣בוּ גשמיהון גֶשְׁמְה֗וֹן דִּ֠י לָֽא־יִפְלְח֤וּן וְלָֽא־יִסְגְּדוּן֙ לְכָל־אֱלָ֔הּ לָהֵ֖ן לֵאלָֽהֲהֽוֹן׃
verses.translit: ʿănēh Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar wə-ʾāmar bərîḵ ʾĕlāhăhōn dî-Šadraḵ Mêšaḵ wa-ʿĂḇēḏ Nəḡō dî-šəlaḥ malʾăḵēh wə-šêziḇ lə-ʿaḇdōhî dī hiṯrəḥiṣū ʿălōhî ū-millat malkāʾ šannîw wî-haḇū ḡešmə-hōn dī lāʾ-yiplə-ḥūn wə-lāʾ-yisgədūn lə-ḵol-ʾĕlāh lāhēn lê-ʾlāhăhōn
verses.notes: **Nebuchadnezzar said: 'Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who has sent his angel and delivered his servants who trusted in him, defying the king's command and yielding their bodies rather than serve and worship any god except their own God.'** **IDENTIFICATION OF THE FOURTH FIGURE — 'his angel'** (מַלְאֲכֵהּ malʾăḵēh): Nebuchadnezzar's own confession identifies the fourth man as YHWH's angel — consistent with the angelic reading of v 25. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Dan 6:23 (the angel-rescue in the lions' den parallels precisely); cf. Acts 12:7-11 (the angel of the Lord delivering Peter from prison).

verses.text: וּמִנִּי֮ שִׂ֣ים טְעֵם֒ דִּי֩ כָל־עַ֨ם אֻמָּ֜ה וְלִשָּׁ֗ן דִּֽי־יֵאמַ֤ר שלה שָׁלוּ֙ עַ֣ל אֱלָהֲה֗וֹן דִּֽי־שַׁדְרַ֤ךְ מֵישַׁךְ֙ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֔וֹא הַדָּמִ֣ין יִתְעֲבֵ֔ד וּבַיְתֵ֖הּ נְוָלִ֣י יִשְׁתַּוֵּ֑ה כָּל־קֳבֵ֗ל דִּ֣י לָ֤א אִיתַי֙ אֱלָ֣ה אָחֳרָ֔ן דִּֽי־יִכֻּ֥ל לְהַצָּלָ֖ה כִּדְנָֽה׃
verses.translit: ū-minnî śîm ṭəʿēm dī ḵol-ʿam ʾummāh wə-liššān dî-yêmar šālū ʿal ʾĕlāhăhōn dî-Šadraḵ Mêšaḵ wa-ʿĂḇēḏ Nəḡō haddāmîn yiṯʿăḇēḏ ū-ḇaytēh nəwālî yištawwēh kol-qŏḇēl dī lāʾ ʾîtay ʾĕlāh ʾoḥŏrān dî-yikkul lə-haṣṣālāh ki-ḏnāh
verses.notes: **'Therefore I make a decree: any people, nation, or language that speaks anything amiss against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego shall be torn limb from limb, and their houses laid in ruins; for there is no other god who is able to deliver in this way.'** **THE GENTILE-CONFESSION FORMULA**: Nebuchadnezzar enacts the Babylonian-imperial-court literary pattern (the foreign king confesses YHWH's supremacy after a miracle). cf. 2:47, 4:34, 6:26.

verses.text: בֵּאדַ֣יִן מַלְכָּ֗א הַצְלַ֛ח לְשַׁדְרַ֥ךְ מֵישַׁ֖ךְ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֑וֹ בִּמְדִינַ֖ת בָּבֶֽל׃
verses.translit: bēʾḏayin malkāʾ haṣlaḥ lə-Šadraḵ Mêšaḵ wa-ʿĂḇēḏ Nəḡō bi-mḏînaṯ Bāḇel
verses.notes: **Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in the province of Babylon.** Narrative-closure: the Joseph-pattern vindication-promotion.
